content.value_statement: Exploratory research changes can drift from baselines and become hard to compare. This skill guides isolated code adaptations and records rollback-aware evidence in explore_outputs.
actual_capabilities: Guides isolated exploratory changes in deep learning research repositories.
Identifies candidate model, config, and training files for review.
Builds a conservative patch plan from repo paths and structured inputs.
Defines smoke checks for syntax, imports, configs, and model surfaces.
Specifies explore_outputs records for changes, comparisons, top runs, and status.
limitations: Requires explicit researcher authorization before exploratory modifications.
Does not verify baseline reproduction or final contribution claims.
Does not manage full exploration campaigns or trusted training execution.
Uses path and keyword heuristics, so selected targets need human review.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Model Adapter
use_cases.description: Plan a small LoRA or adapter insertion on an isolated branch with clear rollback notes.

use_cases.title: Review Candidate Edit Scope
use_cases.description: Find likely model, config, and training touchpoints before making a reversible code change.

use_cases.title: Prepare Exploration Records
use_cases.description: Create consistent change, comparison, top-run, and status records for exploratory implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Authorized Exploration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small candidate change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use explore-code for an authorized exploratory change on an isolated branch. Plan a minimal adapter change and list expected explore_outputs records.

prompt_templates.title: Map Candidate Touchpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using known research context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use current_research as the baseline anchor. Identify likely model, config, and training files for a reversible candidate implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Patch Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with an idea card and analysis hints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the selected idea card and analysis hints. Produce a minimal patch plan, rollback notes, and smoke validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple variant axes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the variant axes to plan bounded code tracks. Keep every track tied to current_research and avoid broad rewrites.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a LoRA adapter experiment on an isolated branch.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a small target list, a reversible patch plan, planned smoke checks, and records to create in explore_outputs.

output_examples.input: A research engineer provides a current_research label and task family.
output_examples.output: The skill narrows candidate files by task keywords and keeps the baseline identifier in every planning note.

output_examples.input: A lab lead wants evidence that exploratory edits stayed separate from trusted results.
output_examples.output: The skill produces expectations for changesets, scientific changelogs, comparability notes, top runs, and status reporting.

best_practices: Use the skill only after explicit approval for exploratory modifications.
Keep all edits on an isolated branch or worktree.
Record rollback steps and comparison anchors before treating results as candidates.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for trusted baseline reproduction.
Do not claim verified research contributions from exploratory outputs.
Do not use it for broad refactors or from-scratch implementations.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It plans and guides authorized exploratory code adaptations in deep learning research repositories.

faq.question: Does it modify the trusted baseline?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires an isolated branch or worktree for exploratory changes.

faq.question: Can it verify a research result?
faq.answer: No. It treats all outputs as candidates until separate validation confirms them.

faq.question: What files does it expect as output?
faq.answer: It expects changeset, scientific changelog, comparability, top-run, and status records under explore_outputs.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users check manually?
faq.answer: Users should review selected target files, rollback plans, and smoke checks before running experiments.
